strings.name: Mate Rimac
strings.role: Rimac founder and Bugatti Rimac CEO
strings.summary: Mate Rimac is a Croatian entrepreneur and innovator born in Livno. He founded Rimac, building teams for high-performance electric cars, batteries and powertrains, and leads Bugatti Rimac. Vehicle, component and manufacturing achievements involve engineering teams and partner companies.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through November 17, 2026. Dated succession announcements take precedence over old titles on undated pages. Equity deals, personal holdings, demonstration cars, customer deliveries and future technology plans are distinguished.
strings.influence.rationale: Founded Rimac, advancing high-performance electric cars, batteries and powertrains and contributing to Europe’s automotive technology industry.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birth and identity
strings.facts.f1.value: Born in 1988 in Livno, now in Bosnia and Herzegovina; the Croatian Encyclopedia identifies him as a Croatian innovator and entrepreneur.
strings.facts.f2.label: Group and subsidiary roles
strings.facts.f2.value: Group releases name him Group President and Bugatti Rimac CEO. Antony Sheriff took over as Group CEO in 2024 and Nurdin Pitarević as Technology CEO in 2026.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Vehicles and components
strings.highlights.h1.text: Combines electric sports-car development with battery and powertrain supply; vehicle performance and production remain team achievements.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Cooperation across brands
strings.highlights.h2.text: Coordinates businesses within Bugatti Rimac, with distinct Bugatti and Rimac brands and production sites; the joint company is not a personal sole proprietorship.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Porsche stake sale completed
strings.timeline.t1.text: Porsche and Bugatti confirm the HOF Capital-led consortium’s acquisition. April signing and September completion are distinct; proceeds are not Rimac’s personal wealth.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Technology CEO succession
strings.timeline.t2.text: Nurdin Pitarević takes over Rimac Technology; Rimac remains Group President and Bugatti Rimac CEO.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Group leadership reorganization
strings.timeline.t3.text: Announcement names Antony Sheriff Group CEO and Rimac President of the Management Board; distinct from the later Technology succession.
strings.timeline.t4.title: First customer Nevera delivered
strings.timeline.t4.text: August 4 release confirms car 001 delivered to Nico Rosberg; publication date is not assumed to be handover date, and the driver’s F1 title is not Rimac’s award.
strings.timeline.t5.title: First production-version Nevera completed
strings.timeline.t5.text: July 12 report records car 000, retained by the company for demonstration and marketing; not yet the first customer delivery.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Leads Bugatti Rimac operations
strings.timeline.t6.text: November 2 release records incorporation and operations on November 1, with Rimac as CEO. Distinct brands and French/Croatian production sites remain.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Founds Greyp Bikes
strings.timeline.t7.text: Croatian Encyclopedia records the electric-bicycle venture; historical founding does not establish current office or ownership.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Founds Rimac Automobili
strings.timeline.t8.text: Develops electric sports cars in Croatia; 2009 founding is distinct from later team expansion, production and group restructuring.
